steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Bind claims to volumes** in *Volumes, PVs, PVCs and StorageClasses*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Your app writes uploaded images to `/app/uploads` inside the container, with no volume. The pod is rescheduled after a node upgrade. What happens to the images?
options: They are gone: they were in the container's writable layer on the old node
They are copied to the new node by the kubelet
steps.explain: Use a PersistentVolumeClaim, or better for uploads, object storage (Blob Storage, S3) so any replica can read them.

steps.title: Rebuild Bind claims to volumes cold
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, string> Bind(List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> claims, List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> volumes)`.

For each claim **in order**, pick an unbound volume with the same `Class`, the same `Mode`, and `SizeGi >= claim.SizeGi`. If several fit, take the **smallest**; ties by name. Map claim name → volume name, or → `"Pending"` if none fits. Each volume binds at most once.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
Dictionary<string, string> Bind(List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> claims, List<(string Name, int SizeGi, string Mode, string Class)> volumes)
